1: //! # pathland-view
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland SwiftUI-style view DSL. Core components (`VStack`, `HStack`,
4: //! `Text`) and decoupled modifiers build a retained **view tree**
5: //! (`pathland_engine::Node`) that the diff emitter in `pathland-core` turns into
6: //! declarative `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes.
7: //!
8: //! ## The three operations
9: //!
10: //! Every concrete view exposes the same three operations, usable at creation or
11: //! chained, in **any order** (spec/DSL.md §2):
12: //!
13: //! - **values** — `Type::with(|c| …)` (static) / `view.with(|c| …)` (chained),
14: //!   where `c` is the view's fluent [`Configurable::Config`].
15: //! - **modifiers** — `Type::modifiers((A, B, …))` / `view.modifiers((A, B, …))`,
16: //!   where the modifiers are passed as a **tuple** (or a single modifier).
17: //! - **children** — `Type::children(vec![…])` / `view.children(vec![…])` on
18: //!   every content-bearing view (and the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros).
19: //!
20: //! ```
21: //! use pathland_view::{vstack, text, View, ViewExt, Children, Padding, FontSize, Align};
22: //!
23: //! let node = VStack::with(|v| { v.spacing(8.0).alignment(Align::Center); })
24: //!     .children(vec![Box::new(text("a")), Box::new(text("b"))])
25: //!     .modifiers((Padding(16.0), FontSize(12.0)))
26: //!     .build();
27: //! # let _ = node;
28: //! # use pathland_view::VStack;
29: //! ```
30: //!
31: //! ## Decoupled modifiers
32: //!
33: //! Modifiers are **decoupled from views** (SwiftUI-style): any modifier applies
34: //! to any view through `modifiers(...)`, and application code composes
35: //! **custom modifiers** from the core ones by implementing `ViewModifier`:
36: //!
37: //! ```
38: //! use pathland_view::{View, ViewExt, ViewModifier, Node, Padding, Background, Color};
39: //!
40: //! struct Card;
41: //! impl ViewModifier for Card {
42: //!     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
43: //!         Padding(16.0).apply(node);
44: //!         Background(Color::argb(0xFF_EEEEEE)).apply(node);
45: //!     }
46: //! }
47: //!
48: //! // Works on any view:
49: //! let a = pathland_view::text("A").modifiers(Card);
50: //! let b = pathland_view::vstack![].modifiers(Card);
51: //! # let _ = (a, b);
52: //! ```
53: //!
54: //! Unsupported combinations are **allowed and ignored**: the modifier emits its
55: //! property and the renderer ignores what it cannot apply.
56: //!
57: //! ## No layout math
58: //!
59: //! The DSL describes structure + constraint properties only. It never computes
60: //! bounds; native renderers lay out their own elements.
61: //!
62: //! This crate is `no_std` + `alloc`.
63:

560: /// A config value that is either a **static** value or a **signal binding**
561: /// (spec DSL.md §2): a static value emits as a plain property; a signal becomes a
562: /// node-level binding that re-emits only that property when it changes. This is
563: /// the Rust realization of "every value member accepts a raw value or a signal".
564: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
565: pub enum Reactive<T> {
566:     /// A raw, non-reactive value.
567:     Static(T),
568:     /// A property bound to a signal.
569:     Signal(SignalId),
570: }
571: 
572: /// Convert a raw value or a signal into a [`Reactive`] config value. Implemented
573: /// for `T` (static) and for `Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>` (binding); the former
574: /// `Bound` modifier folds into this.
575: pub trait IntoReactive<T> {
576:     /// Convert into a [`Reactive`].
577:     fn into_reactive(self) -> Reactive<T>;
578: }
579: 
580: impl<T> IntoReactive<T> for T {
581:     fn into_reactive(self) -> Reactive<T> {
582:         Reactive::Static(self)
583:     }
584: }
585: 
586: impl<T> IntoReactive<T> for Signal<T> {
587:     fn into_reactive(self) -> Reactive<T> {
588:         Reactive::Signal(self.id())
589:     }
590: }
591: 
592: impl<T> IntoReactive<T> for WritableSignal<T> {
593:     fn into_reactive(self) -> Reactive<T> {
594:         Reactive::Signal(self.id())
595:     }
596: }

598: /// Apply a reactive f32 property (static value or signal binding).
599: fn reactive_f32(node: &mut Node, prop: u16, r: &Reactive<f32>) {
600:     match r {
601:         Reactive::Static(v) => {
602:             node.properties.insert(prop, v.to_bits());
603:         }
604:         Reactive::Signal(id) => {
605:             node.property_bindings.insert(prop, *id);
606:         }
607:     }
608: }

681: /// Apply a length property: a literal/signal behaves like [`reactive_f32`]; a
682: /// token reference rides `Node::token_properties` as `DESIGN_TOKEN`.

1065: /// Emits `WIDTH`, `HEIGHT`, and optionally `ALIGNMENT` as ordinary
1066: /// `SET_PROPERTY` values. `width`/`height` use the `size::FILL` (-1.0) and
1067: /// `size::HUG_CONTENT` (-2.0) sentinels; `None` leaves that axis to the native
1068: /// renderer. Infinite values (SwiftUI `maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity`) are
1069: /// normalized to `size::FILL` when applied.

1073:     pub height: Option<f32>,
1074:     pub alignment: Option<Align>,
1075: }

1077: impl Frame {
1078:     /// A frame from optional width/height/alignment.
1079:     pub const fn new(width: Option<f32>, height: Option<f32>, alignment: Option<Align>) -> Self {
1080:         Self {
1081:             width,
1082:             height,
1083:             alignment,
1084:         }
1085:     }
1086: 
1087:     /// A fixed `width` x `height` frame with no alignment.
1088:     pub const fn size(width: f32, height: f32) -> Self {
1089:         Self::new(Some(width), Some(height), None)
1090:     }

1092:     /// A fixed `width` with no height hint.
1093:     pub const fn width(width: f32) -> Self {
1094:         Self::new(Some(width), None, None)
1095:     }
1096: 
1097:     /// A fixed `height` with no width hint.
1098:     pub const fn height(height: f32) -> Self {
1099:         Self::new(None, Some(height), None)
1100:     }
1101: }

1103: impl ViewModifier for Frame {
1104:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
1105:         if let Some(w) = self.width {
1106:             node.properties
1107:                 .insert(property_id::WIDTH, fill_or(w).to_bits());
1108:         }
1109:         if let Some(h) = self.height {
1110:             node.properties

1465: /// type; a `Color::token(..)` reference rides the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type.
1466: fn apply_color(node: &mut Node, prop: u16, color: Color) {

1513: /// Bind an f32-valued property (`VALUE`) to a signal (two-way).
1514: fn bind_value_f32(node: &mut Node, prop: u16, signal: WritableSignal<f32>) {
1515:     let initial = signal.get().unwrap_or(0.0);
1516:     node.properties.insert(prop, initial.to_bits());
1517:     node.property_bindings.insert(prop, signal.id());
1518:     mark_binding(node);

1523: fn bind_value_bool(node: &mut Node, prop: u16, signal: WritableSignal<bool>) {
1524:     let initial = signal.get().unwrap_or(false);
1525:     node.properties.insert(prop, if initial { 1 } else { 0 });
1526:     node.property_bindings.insert(prop, signal.id());
1527:     mark_binding(node);
1528:     node.gestures.push(Gesture::ValueInput(value_sink_bool(signal)));

300: /// Assign stable unique sequential ids to a tree (pre-order; root first).
301: ///
302: /// The engine keys its diff snapshot by node id, so call this after building
303: /// the (possibly re-built) tree and before `Engine::emit`.
304: ///
305: /// **Media controllers are pinned**: a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node keeps the id it
306: /// was first given (spec/MEDIA.md), so a structural swap that shifts other ids
307: /// never changes the playback key — and its `VIDEO` surface's
308: /// `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` is linked in the same pass.
309: pub fn assign_ids(root: &mut Node, next: &mut u32) {
310:     // Reserve every already-pinned controller id up front, so no other node can
311:     // be handed one even when it is lower than the current cursor.
312:     let mut reserved = BTreeSet::new();
313:     collect_pinned_controller_ids(root, &mut reserved);
314:     assign_ids_pass(root, next, &mut reserved);
315: }
316: 
317: /// Collect the ids already pinned by the controllers present in this tree.
318: fn collect_pinned_controller_ids(node: &Node, out: &mut BTreeSet<u32>) {
319:     if matches!(node.component, Component::MediaController) {
320:         if let Some(id) = node
321:             .media_controller
322:             .as_ref()
323:             .map(|c| c.0.pinned_node_id())
324:             .filter(|id| *id != 0)
325:         {
326:             out.insert(id);
327:         }
328:     }
329:     for child in &node.children {
330:         collect_pinned_controller_ids(child, out);
331:     }
332: }
333: 
334: /// Take the next free (unreserved) id from the cursor.
335: fn take_id(next: &mut u32, reserved: &BTreeSet<u32>) -> u32 {
336:     if *next == 0 {
337:         *next = 1;
338:     }
339:     while reserved.contains(next) {
340:         *next += 1;
341:     }
342:     let id = *next;
343:     *next += 1;
344:     id
345: }
346: 
347: fn assign_ids_pass(node: &mut Node, next: &mut u32, reserved: &mut BTreeSet<u32>) {
348:     match (&node.component, node.media_controller.clone()) {
349:         (Component::MediaController, Some(controller)) => {
350:             // A controller keeps the id it was first pinned to.
351:             let pinned = controller.0.pinned_node_id();
352:             node.id = if pinned != 0 {
353:                 pinned
354:             } else {
355:                 let id = take_id(next, reserved);
356:                 controller.0.pin_node_id(id);
357:                 id
358:             };
359:             reserved.insert(node.id);
360:         }
361:         _ => {
362:             node.id = take_id(next, reserved);
363:         }
364:     }
365:     // Link a video surface to its controller (spec/MEDIA.md).
366:     if matches!(node.component, Component::Video) {
367:         if let Some(id) = node
368:             .media_controller
369:             .as_ref()
370:             .map(|c| c.0.pinned_node_id())
371:             .filter(|id| *id != 0)
372:         {
373:             node.properties.insert(property_id::MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID, id);
374:         }
375:     }
376:     for child in &mut node.children {
377:         assign_ids_pass(child, next, reserved);
378:     }
379: }

381: /// Collect a `node id -> tap callback` map from a built (and id-assigned) tree.
382: ///
383: /// Call after [`assign_ids`] so each node has its stable id; the returned map
384: /// keys the recognizer's tap target to the closure registered by
385: /// `.on_tap_gesture(...)`.
386: pub fn collect_tap_handlers(root: &Node, out: &mut BTreeMap<u32, TapHandler>) {
387:     for gesture in &root.gestures {
388:         if let Gesture::Tap(handler) = gesture {
389:             out.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
390:         }
391:     }
392:     for child in &root.children {
393:         collect_tap_handlers(child, out);
394:     }
395: }

398: /// keyed by node id. A host routes the control events into these:
399: /// `TEXT_CHANGED` → [`InputHandlers::text`], `VALUE_CHANGED` →
400: /// [`InputHandlers::value`], `DATE_CHANGED` → [`InputHandlers::date`]. Each sink
401: /// writes its bound signal; re-emit the tree afterwards to flush the delta.

404:     /// `TEXT_CHANGED` sinks (text fields / editors).
405:     pub text: BTreeMap<u32, TextInputHandler>,
406:     /// `VALUE_CHANGED` sinks (toggle / slider / stepper / picker / color picker).
407:     pub value: BTreeMap<u32, ValueInputHandler>,
408:     /// `DATE_CHANGED` sinks (date pickers).
409:     pub date: BTreeMap<u32, DateInputHandler>,
410: }
411: 
412: /// Collect the two-way binding sinks from a built (and id-assigned) tree.
413: pub fn collect_input_handlers(root: &Node, out: &mut InputHandlers) {
414:     for gesture in &root.gestures {
415:         match gesture {
416:             Gesture::TextInput(handler) => {
417:                 out.text.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
418:             }
419:             Gesture::ValueInput(handler) => {
420:                 out.value.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
421:             }
422:             Gesture::DateInput(handler) => {
423:                 out.date.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
424:             }
425:             Gesture::Tap(_) => {}
426:         }
427:     }
428:     for child in &root.children {
429:         collect_input_handlers(child, out);
430:     }

1: //! Diff-based reactive emitter.
2: //!
3: //! The engine holds the application's retained view tree and emits the
4: //! declarative structure as `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes into the 16-byte ring
5: //! buffer (VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment). It does not
6: //! compute rects or layout; native renderers lay out their own elements.
7: //!
8: //! Emission is diff-based: on each `emit` the engine compares the current tree
9: //! against a snapshot of what it last emitted and writes only the opcodes for
10: //! nodes that actually changed. An unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
11: //!
12: //! The emit pass performs zero dynamic heap allocations in the steady state.
13: //!
14: //! ## Signals
15: //!
16: //! Nodes may bind their text or a property to a [`crate::SignalId`]. The engine
17: //! resolves those bindings during emit (recording the dependency) and re-emits
18: //! only the affected nodes on [`Engine::set_signal`] — no full tree walk.
19:

33: /// Encode a `LIST` property's arena entry: `[u32 count][f32 × count]`
34: /// (spec/OPCODE.md §Value types — a `FIT_QUERY` threshold table).
35: fn encode_list(values: &[f32]) -> Vec<u8> {
36:     let mut bytes = vec![0u8; 4 + 4 * values.len()];
37:     bytes[0..4].copy_from_slice(&(values.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
38:     for (i, value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
39:         let o = 4 + 4 * i;
40:         bytes[o..o + 4].copy_from_slice(&value.to_bits().to_le_bytes());
41:     }
42:     bytes
43: }

54:     /// arena offset is reused across passes so an unchanged string never
55:     /// re-allocates into the bump arena.
56:     string_properties: BTreeMap<u16, (String, u32)>,

58:     /// arena offset is reused across passes so an unchanged list never

61:     /// Last-emitted `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs: property → (token path, arena offset).
62:     /// The arena offset is reused across passes so an unchanged ref never

76: /// The diff-based reactive emitter.
77: ///
78: /// `Engine` keeps the snapshot of what was last emitted and owns the signal
79: /// store. Calling `emit` with a (possibly mutated) retained tree writes only
80: /// the delta opcodes; `set_signal` writes deltas for only the bound nodes.
81: pub struct Engine {
82:     /// nodeId to last emitted state (a preallocated slab; node ids are dense).
83:     snapshot: Vec<Option<SnapshotNode>>,
84:     /// Monotonic generation stamp for the current pass.
85:     gen: u64,
86:     /// Reactive signal runtime (values + computed/effects + node dependencies).
87:     store: Runtime,
88:     /// Window/surface metadata signal bindings (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`).
89:     window: WindowMetadata,
90:     /// The last window metadata written to the wire (dedupe / clear detection).
91:     window_emitted: WindowMeta,
92: }

100: impl Engine {
101:     pub fn new() -> Self {
102:         Self {
103:             snapshot: Vec::new(),
104:             gen: 0,
105:             store: Runtime::new(),
106:             window: WindowMetadata::new(),
107:             window_emitted: WindowMeta::new(),
108:         }
109:     }

111:     /// The shared reactive runtime (for creating typed signals / computeds).
112:     pub fn runtime(&self) -> Runtime {
113:         self.store.clone()
114:     }

116:     /// Reconcile `root` against the snapshot, emitting only changed opcodes.
117:     pub fn emit(
118:         &mut self,
119:         root: &Node,
120:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
121:     ) -> Result<EmitResult, pathland_core::RingError> {
122:         self.gen = self.gen.wrapping_add(1);
123:         // Rebuild the signal->node dependency index from scratch; reconcile
124:         // re-adds the bindings this tree actually uses, so stale subscriptions
125:         // vanish.
126:         self.store.clear_node_deps();
127:         // Window metadata is renderer-global, not part of the tree: emit the
128:         // initial values (and any rebind/clear) before the node opcodes.
129:         let mut out = self.emit_window_metadata(guest)?;
130:         self.reconcile_node(root, None, 0, guest, &mut out)?;
131: 
132:         for (id, slot) in self.snapshot.iter_mut().enumerate() {
133:             if let Some(s) = slot {
134:                 if s.gen != self.gen {
135:                     if let Some(parent) = s.parent {
136:                         guest.remove_child(parent, id as u32)?;
137:                         out += 1;
138:                     }
139:                     guest.delete_node(id as u32)?;
140:                     out += 1;
141:                     *slot = None;
142:                 }
143:             }
144:         }
145:         Ok(EmitResult { opcodes: out })
146:     }

148:     /// Number of nodes tracked in the snapshot (diagnostics).
149:     pub fn tracked_nodes(&self) -> usize {

153:     /// Bind the window/surface presentation metadata
154:     /// (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`): title, description, locale. Values are
155:     /// signal-backed, so a route can drive them from a computed. The next
156:     /// [`Engine::emit`] writes the initial values; a subsequent
157:     /// [`Engine::set_signal`] writes only the changed field.
158:     pub fn bind_window_metadata(&mut self, metadata: WindowMetadata) {
159:         self.window = metadata;
160:     }

162:     /// Bind one window-metadata field to a signal (the flat/C-ABI form of
163:     /// [`Engine::bind_window_metadata`]).
164:     pub fn bind_window_field(&mut self, field: u16, signal: SignalId) {
165:         self.window.set_signal(field, signal);
166:     }

168:     /// Emit changed window-metadata fields. Unchanged fields write nothing; a
169:     /// field that became unset writes an empty string (clear).
170:     fn emit_window_metadata(
171:         &mut self,
172:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
173:     ) -> Result<usize, pathland_core::RingError> {
174:         let mut out = 0usize;
175:         for field in window_field::ALL {
176:             let value = self.window.signal(field).and_then(|id| {
177:                 let value = self.store.get(id);
178:                 value.to_text().map(ToOwned::to_owned)
179:             });
180:             let previous = self.window_emitted.get(field).map(ToOwned::to_owned);
181:             if value == previous {
182:                 continue;
183:             }
184:             let text = value.as_deref().unwrap_or("");
185:             let offset = guest.alloc_str(text).map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
186:             guest.push_opcode(Opcode::new(
187:                 category::META,
188:                 meta::SET_WINDOW_METADATA,
189:                 0,
190:                 field as u32,
191:                 offset,
192:                 0,
193:             ))?;
194:             self.window_emitted.set(field, text);
195:             out += 1;
196:         }
197:         Ok(out)
198:     }

200:     /// Emit a global design-token override (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`).
201:     /// Overrides are renderer-global and apply everywhere the renderer resolves
202:     /// tokens; a `dark.`-prefixed path overrides the dark variant
203:     /// (spec/TOKENS.md). Returns the arena offset of the token path.
204:     pub fn set_design_token(
205:         &mut self,
206:         path: &str,
207:         value_type: u8,
208:         value: u32,
209:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
210:     ) -> Result<u32, pathland_core::RingError> {
211:         guest.set_design_token(path, value_type, value)
212:     }

214:     /// Emit a batch of global design-token overrides ([`Theme`](crate::Theme))
215:     /// as `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcodes. `STRING`-valued overrides allocate
216:     /// their value into the guest arena first (the wire carries an arena ref).
217:     ///
218:     /// Overrides are renderer-global: they never re-emit nodes and are not part
219:     /// of the diff. Emit once at mount, before the tree.
220:     pub fn apply_theme(
221:         &mut self,
222:         theme: &crate::Theme,
223:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
224:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
225:         for (path, value) in theme.iter() {
226:             self.emit_token_override(path, value, guest)?;
227:         }
228:         Ok(())
229:     }

231:     /// Emit an adaptive theme ([`AdaptiveTheme`](crate::AdaptiveTheme)): the
232:     /// **light** theme's overrides as base tokens, the **dark** theme's with the
233:     /// `dark.` scheme prefix (spec/TOKENS.md).
234:     pub fn apply_adaptive_theme(
235:         &mut self,
236:         adaptive: &crate::AdaptiveTheme,
237:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
238:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
239:         self.apply_theme(&adaptive.light, guest)?;
240:         for (path, value) in adaptive.dark.iter() {
241:             let dark_path = if path.starts_with("dark.") {
242:                 path.to_string()
243:             } else {
244:                 alloc::format!("dark.{path}")
245:             };
246:             self.emit_token_override(&dark_path, value, guest)?;
247:         }
248:         Ok(())
249:     }

251:     /// Emit `META::RESET_THEME` (clear every application token override; the
252:     /// renderer falls back to its defaults). A replacement theme emits this
253:     /// immediately before its overrides in the same frame.

255:         &mut self,
256:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
257:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {

261:     /// Emit `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME`: force light/dark or restore platform

265:         &mut self,
266:         mode: crate::ColorSchemeMode,
267:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
268:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
269:         guest.push_opcode(Opcode::new(
270:             category::META,
271:             meta::SET_COLOR_SCHEME,
272:             0,
273:             mode.code(),
274:             0,
275:             0,
276:         ))
277:     }

279:     /// Replace the theme at runtime: `RESET_THEME` then the new overrides in
280:     /// one frame (spec/DSL.md §7.3).

282:         &mut self,

300:     /// Emit one `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override, arena-allocating STRING values.
301:     fn emit_token_override(
302:         &mut self,
303:         path: &str,
304:         value: &pathland_core::tokens::TokenValue,
305:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
306:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
307:         use pathland_core::tokens::TokenValue;
308:         match value {
309:             TokenValue::Str(s) => {
310:                 let ref_ = guest
311:                     .alloc_str(s)
312:                     .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
313:                 guest.set_design_token(path, value.value_type(), ref_)?;
314:             }
315:             _ => {
316:                 if let Some(bits) = value.to_bits() {
317:                     guest.set_design_token(path, value.value_type(), bits)?;
318:                 }
319:             }
320:         }
321:         Ok(())
322:     }

351:     /// Write a typed writable signal and re-emit only the nodes bound to it.
352:     pub fn set<T: SignalValueKind>(
353:         &mut self,
354:         signal: WritableSignal<T>,
355:         value: T,
356:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
357:     ) -> Result<usize, pathland_core::RingError> {

364:     }

366:     /// Replace a signal's value and re-emit only the nodes that depend on it
367:     /// (including nodes bound to any computed signal it feeds).
368:     ///
369:     /// Writes `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` deltas for the bound nodes whose
370:     /// materialized value changed. Returns the number of opcodes written.
371:     pub fn set_signal(
372:         &mut self,
373:         id: SignalId,
374:         value: SignalValue,
375:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
376:     ) -> Result<usize, pathland_core::RingError> {
377:         let changed = self.store.set(id, value);
378:         let mut out = 0usize;
379:         for cell in changed {
380:             out += self.emit_cell(cell, guest)?;
381:         }
382:         // A window-metadata signal (or a computed feeding one) changed. Fields
383:         // are compared, so an unrelated signal emits zero opcodes.
384:         out += self.emit_window_metadata(guest)?;
385:         Ok(out)
386:     }

388:     /// Re-emit the node bindings on one (changed) signal.
389:     fn emit_cell(
390:         &mut self,
391:         id: SignalId,
392:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
393:     ) -> Result<usize, pathland_core::RingError> {
394:         let deps: Vec<Dep> = self.store.node_deps(id);
395:         if deps.is_empty() {
396:             return Ok(0);
397:         }
398:         let value = self.store.get(id);
399:         let mut out = 0usize;
400:         for dep in deps {
401:             match dep {
402:                 Dep::Text { node } => {
403:                     let new_text: Option<String> = value.to_text().map(ToOwned::to_owned);
404:                     let prev_text = self.snapshot_text(node);
405:                     if new_text.as_deref() != prev_text {
406:                         if let Some(t) = new_text.as_deref() {
407:                             guest.set_text(node, t)?;
408:                             out += 1;
409:                         }
410:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
411:                             s.text = new_text;
412:                         }
413:                     }
414:                 }
415:                 Dep::Property { node, prop } => {
416:                     let new_value = value.to_property_u32();
417:                     let prev_value = self.snapshot_property(node, prop);
418:                     if new_value != prev_value {
419:                         if let Some(v) = new_value {
420:                             guest.set_property(node, prop, value_type_for(prop), v)?;
421:                             out += 1;
422:                         }
423:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
424:                             match new_value {
425:                                 Some(v) => {
426:                                     s.properties.insert(prop, v);
427:                                 }
428:                                 None => {
429:                                     s.properties.remove(&prop);
430:                                 }
431:                             }
432:                         }
433:                     }
434:                 }
435:                 Dep::StringProperty { node, prop } => {
436:                     let new_text: Option<String> = value.to_text().map(ToOwned::to_owned);
437:                     let prev_text = self.snapshot_string(node, prop).map(ToOwned::to_owned);
438:                     if new_text != prev_text {
439:                         let emitted = match new_text.as_deref() {
440:                             Some(t) => {
441:                                 let arena = guest
442:                                     .alloc_str(t)
443:                                     .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
444:                                 guest.set_property(node, prop, value_type::STRING, arena)?;
445:                                 out += 1;
446:                                 Some((t.to_string(), arena))
447:                             }
448:                             None => None,
449:                         };
450:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
451:                             match emitted {
452:                                 Some((v, arena)) => {
453:                                     s.string_properties.insert(prop, (v, arena));
454:                                 }
455:                                 None => {
456:                                     s.string_properties.remove(&prop);
457:                                 }
458:                             }
459:                         }
460:                     }
461:                 }
462:             }
463:         }
464:         Ok(out)
465:     }

467:     fn snapshot_mut(&mut self, node: u32) -> Option<&mut SnapshotNode> {
468:         self.snapshot
469:             .get_mut(node as usize)
470:             .and_then(|s| s.as_mut())
471:     }
472: 
473:     fn snapshot_text(&self, node: u32) -> Option<&str> {
474:         self.snapshot
475:             .get(node as usize)
476:             .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
477:             .and_then(|s| s.text.as_deref())
478:     }
479: 
480:     fn snapshot_property(&self, node: u32, prop: u16) -> Option<u32> {
481:         self.snapshot
482:             .get(node as usize)
483:             .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
484:             .and_then(|s| s.properties.get(&prop).copied())
485:     }
486: 
487:     fn snapshot_string(&self, node: u32, prop: u16) -> Option<&str> {
488:         self.snapshot
489:             .get(node as usize)
490:             .and_then(|s| s.as_ref())
491:             .and_then(|s| s.string_properties.get(&prop))
492:             .map(|(value, _)| value.as_str())
493:     }

495:     fn slot_mut(&mut self, id: u32) -> &mut Option<SnapshotNode> {
496:         let idx = id as usize;
497:         if self.snapshot.len() <= idx {
498:             self.snapshot.resize(idx + 1, None);
499:         }
500:         &mut self.snapshot[idx]
501:     }

503:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
504:     fn reconcile_node(
505:         &mut self,
506:         node: &Node,
507:         parent: Option<u32>,
508:         index: usize,
509:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
510:         out: &mut usize,
511:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
512:         let component_type = component_type_id(&node.component);
513: 
514:         // Resolve bindings (owned) before taking the mutable snapshot borrow.
515:         let bound_text: Option<String> = node
516:             .text_binding
517:             .map(|sid| self.store.get(sid))
518:             .and_then(|v| v.to_text().map(ToOwned::to_owned));
519: 
520:         let merged_props: Option<BTreeMap<u16, u32>> = if node.property_bindings.is_empty() {
521:             None
522:         } else {
523:             let mut m = node.properties.clone();
524:             for (prop, sid) in &node.property_bindings {
525:                 if let Some(v) = self.store.get(*sid).to_property_u32() {
526:                     m.insert(*prop, v);
527:                 }
528:             }
529:             Some(m)
530:         };
531: 
532:         // `STRING`-valued property bindings (e.g. a media controller's
533:         // `MEDIA_SOURCE`) resolve on top of the static string properties.
534:         let merged_strings: Option<BTreeMap<u16, String>> = if node.string_bindings.is_empty() {
535:             None
536:         } else {
537:             let mut m = node.string_properties.clone();
538:             for (prop, sid) in &node.string_bindings {
539:                 if let Some(v) = self.store.get(*sid).to_text() {
540:                     m.insert(*prop, v.to_string());
541:                 }
542:             }
543:             Some(m)
544:         };
545: 
546:         let text_borrowed: Option<&str> = match (&bound_text, &node.component) {
547:             (Some(s), _) => Some(s.as_str()),
548:             (None, Component::Text { text }) => Some(text.as_str()),
549:             (None, Component::Button { label }) => Some(label.as_str()),
550:             _ => None,
551:         };
552:         let props: &BTreeMap<u16, u32> = merged_props.as_ref().unwrap_or(&node.properties);
553:         let token_refs = &node.token_properties;
554:         let strings: &BTreeMap<u16, String> = merged_strings
555:             .as_ref()
556:             .unwrap_or(&node.string_properties);
557:         let lists = &node.list_properties;
558: 
559:         let prev = self.slot_mut(node.id).take();
560:         let token_changed = match &prev {
561:             Some(p) => p.token_refs.len() != token_refs.len()
562:                 || p.token_refs
563:                     .iter()
564:                     .any(|(prop, (old, _))| token_refs.get(prop) != Some(old)),
565:             None => !token_refs.is_empty(),
566:         };
567:         let strings_changed = match &prev {
568:             Some(p) => {
569:                 p.string_properties.len() != strings.len()
570:                     || p.string_properties
571:                         .iter()
572:                         .any(|(prop, (old, _))| strings.get(prop) != Some(old))
573:             }
574:             None => !strings.is_empty(),
575:         };
576:         let lists_changed = match &prev {
577:             Some(p) => {
578:                 p.list_properties.len() != lists.len()
579:                     || p.list_properties
580:                         .iter()
581:                         .any(|(prop, (old, _))| lists.get(prop) != Some(old))
582:             }
583:             None => !lists.is_empty(),
584:         };
585:         let props_changed = match &prev {
586:             Some(p) => &p.properties != props || token_changed || strings_changed || lists_changed,
587:             None => !props.is_empty() || !token_refs.is_empty() || !strings.is_empty() || !lists.is_empty(),
588:         };
589:         let text_changed = match &prev {
590:             Some(p) => p.text.as_deref() != text_borrowed,
591:             None => text_borrowed.is_some(),
592:         };
593: 
594:         // Token-ref emission. Built only on mount or when a ref changed, so a
595:         // steady-state pass performs no heap allocations (the unchanged refs'
596:         // arena offsets are reused from the previous snapshot below).
597:         let mut token_emit: Option<BTreeMap<u16, (String, u32)>> = None;
598:         // String-property emission, built only on mount / when a value changed
599:         // (arena offsets reused from the previous snapshot otherwise).
600:         let mut string_emit: Option<BTreeMap<u16, (String, u32)>> = None;
601:         // List-property emission, built only on mount / when a value changed
602:         // (arena offsets reused from the previous snapshot otherwise).
603:         let mut list_emit: Option<BTreeMap<u16, (Vec<f32>, u32)>> = None;
604: 
605:         // Properties in two passes — literals (skipping token-ref'd ids) then
606:         // token refs — so the steady-state emit performs no heap allocations.
607:         match &prev {
608:             None => {
609:                 guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
610:                 *out += 1;
611:                 if let Some(p) = parent {
612:                     guest.insert_child(p, node.id, index as u32)?;
613:                     *out += 1;
614:                 }
615:                 for (prop, value) in props {
616:                     if token_refs.contains_key(prop) {
617:                         continue;
618:                     }
619:                     guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
620:                     *out += 1;
621:                 }
622:                 if !token_refs.is_empty() {
623:                     let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
624:                     for (prop, path) in token_refs {
625:                         let arena = guest
626:                             .alloc_str(path)
627:                             .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
628:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN, arena)?;
629:                         *out += 1;
630:                         m.insert(*prop, (path.clone(), arena));
631:                     }
632:                     token_emit = Some(m);
633:                 }
634:                 if !strings.is_empty() {
635:                     let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
636:                     for (prop, value) in strings {
637:                         let arena = guest
638:                             .alloc_str(value)
639:                             .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
640:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type::STRING, arena)?;
641:                         *out += 1;
642:                         m.insert(*prop, (value.clone(), arena));
643:                     }
644:                     string_emit = Some(m);
645:                 }
646:                 if !lists.is_empty() {
647:                     let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
648:                     for (prop, values) in lists {
649:                         let bytes = encode_list(values);
650:                         let arena = guest
651:                             .alloc(&bytes)
652:                             .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
653:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type::LIST, arena)?;
654:                         *out += 1;
655:                         m.insert(*prop, (values.clone(), arena));
656:                     }
657:                     list_emit = Some(m);
658:                 }
659:                 if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
660:                     guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
661:                     *out += 1;
662:                 }
663:             }
664:             Some(p) => {
665:                 if p.parent != parent {
666:                     if let Some(old) = p.parent {
667:                         guest.remove_child(old, node.id)?;
668:                         *out += 1;
669:                     }
670:                     if let Some(new) = parent {
671:                         guest.insert_child(new, node.id, index as u32)?;
672:                         *out += 1;
673:                     }
674:                 } else if p.index != index {
675:                     if let Some(par) = parent {
676:                         guest.move_child(par, node.id, index as u32)?;
677:                         *out += 1;
678:                     }
679:                 }
680:                 if p.component_type != component_type {
681:                     guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
682:                     *out += 1;
683:                 }
684:                 if text_changed {
685:                     if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
686:                         guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
687:                         *out += 1;
688:                     }
689:                 }
690:                 for (prop, value) in props {
691:                     if token_refs.contains_key(prop) {
692:                         continue;
693:                     }
694:                     if p.properties.get(prop) != Some(value) {
695:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
696:                         *out += 1;
697:                     }
698:                 }
699:                 if token_changed {
700:                     let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
701:                     for (prop, path) in token_refs {
702:                         let (arena, changed) = match p.token_refs.get(prop) {
703:                             Some((old_path, old_offset)) if old_path == path => (*old_offset, false),
704:                             _ => {
705:                                 let offset = guest
706:                                     .alloc_str(path)
707:                                     .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
708:                                 (offset, true)
709:                             }
710:                         };
711:                         m.insert(*prop, (path.clone(), arena));
712:                         if changed {
713:                             guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN, arena)?;
714:                             *out += 1;
715:                         }
716:                     }
717:                     token_emit = Some(m);
718:                 }
719:                 if strings_changed {
720:                     let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
721:                     for (prop, value) in strings {
722:                         let (arena, changed) = match p.string_properties.get(prop) {
723:                             Some((old_value, old_offset)) if old_value == value => {
724:                                 (*old_offset, false)
725:                             }
726:                             _ => {
727:                                 let offset = guest

1: //! Reactive signals (Angular-style).
2: //!
3: //! A signal is a piece of application state owned by the shared [`Runtime`].
4: //! Retained tree nodes bind their text or a property to a signal via
5: //! [`SignalId`]; the engine records those dependencies during emission, so when
6: //! a signal's value changes, only the nodes that read it re-emit their deltas.
7: //!
8: //! ## Reactive runtime
9: //!
10: //! [`Runtime`] owns an `Rc<RefCell<Store>>` shared with the typed handles
11: //! ([`Signal`]/[`WritableSignal`]) and with the [`Engine`](crate::Engine). It
12: //! supports **computed** (derived, lazily recomputed, equality-suppressed) and
13: //! **effect** (runs immediately, then on dependency change) signals, plus
14: //! `untracked` reads. Because `pathland-engine` is `no_std` (no thread-local),
15: //! the "current computation" is an explicit stack inside the store — the
16: //! single-threaded equivalent of the Java DSL's thread-local reactive context.
17: //!
18: //! Signals live here (in `no_std` core) so any host — Rust, the native C ABI,
19: //! a future WASM/browser guest — shares the same reactive runtime.

28: /// A signal's value: one of the protocol value kinds.
29: ///
30: /// Property bindings pack to a `SET_PROPERTY` value (u32); text bindings use
31: /// [`SignalValue::Str`]. The richer kinds (`Bool`, `Enum`) are ergonomic typing
32: /// at the host boundary — they still collapse onto the wire's `u32` value.
33: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
34: pub enum SignalValue {
35:     /// A float property (spacing, font_size, padding, opacity, size hints…).
36:     F32(f32),
37:     /// A raw u32 property (color `0xAARRGGBB`, an `EVENT_LISTENERS` mask, …).
38:     U32(u32),
39:     /// A boolean property (visible, clips_to_bounds, …).
40:     Bool(bool),
41:     /// An enum property wire value (alignment, text alignment, truncation, …).
42:     Enum(u8),
43:     /// A string (text content, font family).
44:     Str(String),
45: }

47: impl SignalValue {
48:     /// Pack this value as a `SET_PROPERTY` `u32` value. `None` for [`Str`],
49:     /// which is only valid for text bindings.
50:     ///
51:     /// `Bool` packs as a raw `0`/`1` (the boolean properties are `U8`);
52:     /// `Enum` packs as the enum code widened to an F32 bit pattern (the enum
53:     /// properties are `F32`).
54:     pub fn to_property_u32(&self) -> Option<u32> {
55:         match self {
56:             SignalValue::F32(f) => Some(f.to_bits()),
57:             SignalValue::U32(u) => Some(*u),
58:             SignalValue::Bool(b) => Some(if *b { 1 } else { 0 }),
59:             SignalValue::Enum(e) => Some((*e as f32).to_bits()),
60:             SignalValue::Str(_) => None,
61:         }
62:     }

64:     /// The text for a text binding. `None` for non-`Str` values.
65:     pub fn to_text(&self) -> Option<&str> {
66:         match self {
67:             SignalValue::Str(s) => Some(s.as_str()),
68:             _ => None,
69:         }
70:     }
71: }

259:         store.cells.push(Cell {
260:             value: SignalValue::U32(0),

276:     /// signal it reads changes.
277:     pub fn effect(&self, run: impl Fn() + 'static) {
278:         let run: Rc<dyn Fn()> = Rc::new(run);
279:         let idx = {
280:             let mut store = self.store.borrow_mut();
281:             let idx = store.effects.len();
282:             store.effects.push(EffectCell {
283:                 run,
284:                 sources: Vec::new(),

309:     /// Record that computation `top` reads signal `s` (idempotent).
310:     fn record(store: &mut Store, top: Computation, s: usize) {
311:         match top {
312:             Computation::Signal(t) if t != s => {
313:                 if !store.cells[t].sources.contains(&s) {
314:                     store.cells[t].sources.push(s);
315:                 }
316:                 if !store.cells[s].subscribers.contains(&Subscriber::Signal(t)) {
317:                     store.cells[s].subscribers.push(Subscriber::Signal(t));
318:                 }
319:             }
320:             Computation::Effect(e) => {
321:                 if !store.effects[e].sources.contains(&s) {
322:                     store.effects[e].sources.push(s);
323:                 }
324:                 if !store.cells[s].subscribers.contains(&Subscriber::Effect(e)) {
325:                     store.cells[s].subscribers.push(Subscriber::Effect(e));
326:                 }
327:             }
328:             _ => {}
329:         }
330:     }

332:     /// Ensure a computed cell is up to date (evaluate it if dirty/uninitialized).
333:     fn ensure(&self, idx: usize) {
334:         let compute = {
335:             let store = self.store.borrow();
336:             match store.cells.get(idx) {
337:                 Some(cell) if cell.compute.is_some() && (cell.dirty || !cell.initialized) => {
338:                     cell.compute.clone()
339:                 }
340:                 _ => return,
341:             }
342:         };
343:         let Some(compute) = compute else { return };
344: 
345:         // Cycle guard: if this computed is already on the stack, leave it stale.
346:         {
347:             let mut store = self.store.borrow_mut();
348:             if store.stack.contains(&Computation::Signal(idx)) {
349:                 return;
350:             }
351:             store.stack.push(Computation::Signal(idx));
352:         }
353: 
354:         // Evaluate with no borrow held (the closure reads signals via `get`).
355:         let value = compute();
356: 
357:         {
358:             let mut store = self.store.borrow_mut();
359:             let cell = &mut store.cells[idx];
360:             cell.value = value;
361:             cell.dirty = false;
362:             cell.initialized = true;
363:             store.stack.pop();
364:         }
365:     }

367:     /// Set a signal's value. Marks and recomputes dependent computeds, runs
368:     /// affected effects, and returns the ids of the signals whose value the
369:     /// caller must re-emit (the set signal plus any computed that changed).
370:     pub fn set(&self, id: SignalId, value: SignalValue) -> Vec<SignalId> {
371:         let idx = id.0 as usize;
372:         {
373:             let mut store = self.store.borrow_mut();
374:             let cell = &mut store.cells[idx];
375:             if cell.initialized && cell.value == value {
376:                 return Vec::new();
377:             }
378:             cell.value = value;
379:             cell.initialized = true;
380:         }
381: 
382:         // Propagate: mark computed subscribers dirty (transitively), collect
383:         // effects to run.
384:         let mut dirty: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
385:         let mut effects: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
386:         {
387:             let mut store = self.store.borrow_mut();
388:             let subs = store.cells[idx].subscribers.clone();
389:             let mut queue: Vec<Subscriber> = subs;
390:             while let Some(sub) = queue.pop() {
391:                 match sub {
392:                     Subscriber::Signal(s) => {
393:                         if !dirty.contains(&s) {
394:                             dirty.push(s);
395:                             store.cells[s].dirty = true;
396:                             store.cells[s].sources.clear();
397:                             queue.extend(store.cells[s].subscribers.clone());
398:                         }
399:                     }
400:                     Subscriber::Effect(e) => {
401:                         if !effects.contains(&e) {
402:                             effects.push(e);
403:                         }
404:                     }
405:                 }
406:             }
407:         }
408: 
409:         // Recompute dirty computeds and note which actually changed.
410:         let mut changed: Vec<SignalId> = vec![id];
411:         for d in dirty {
412:             let before = self.store.borrow().cells[d].value.clone();
413:             self.ensure(d);
414:             let after = self.store.borrow().cells[d].value.clone();
415:             if before != after {
416:                 changed.push(SignalId(d as u32));
417:             }
418:         }
419: 
420:         // Synchronous effect flush.
421:         for e in effects {
422:             self.run_effect(e);
423:         }
424: 
425:         changed
426:     }

428:     /// Run an effect (with dependency tracking), rebuilding its sources.
429:     fn run_effect(&self, idx: usize) {
430:         let run = {
431:             let mut store = self.store.borrow_mut();
432:             store.effects[idx].sources.clear();
433:             store.effects[idx].run.clone()
434:         };
435:         {
436:             let mut store = self.store.borrow_mut();
437:             if store.stack.contains(&Computation::Effect(idx)) {
438:                 return; // re-entrant effect write: skip
439:             }
440:             store.stack.push(Computation::Effect(idx));
441:         }
442:         run();
443:         self.store.borrow_mut().stack.pop();
444:     }

1: //! Bump arena for variable-length data in linear memory.
2: //!
3: //! Every entry is self-describing: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`. Opcodes
4: //! reference entries by their byte offset (`arenaRef`), so the entry length is
5: //! read directly from the arena and every opcode stays 16 bytes.
6: 
7: use crate::memory::header;
8: 
9: /// Errors produced by the arena.
10: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
11: pub enum ArenaError {
12:     /// Not enough remaining bytes for the allocation.
13:     OutOfSpace,
14:     /// The arena offset is out of bounds or points to an invalid entry.
15:     InvalidOffset,
16: }
17: 
18: /// Allocate `bytes` into the arena region, returning its byte offset.
19: ///
20: /// The cursor lives in the header block (`OFF_ARENA_CURSOR`).
21: #[inline]
22: pub(crate) fn alloc(data: &mut [u8], header: &mut [u8], bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
23:     alloc_at(data, header, crate::memory::OFF_ARENA_CURSOR, bytes)
24: }
25: 
26: /// Allocate `bytes` into the host → guest (event) arena region, returning its
27: /// byte offset. The cursor lives in the header block
28: /// (`OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR`, host-owned) — the host writes event string
29: /// payloads here so the guest can resolve them over the shared ring.
30: #[inline]
31: pub(crate) fn alloc_event(
32:     data: &mut [u8],
33:     header: &mut [u8],
34:     bytes: &[u8],
35: ) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
36:     alloc_at(data, header, crate::memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR, bytes)
37: }
38: 
39: /// Allocate into any arena region, using the given header cursor offset.
40: #[inline]
41: pub(crate) fn alloc_at(
42:     data: &mut [u8],
43:     header: &mut [u8],
44:     cursor_off: usize,
45:     bytes: &[u8],
46: ) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
47:     let cursor = header::get_u32(header, cursor_off) as usize;
48:     let len = bytes.len();
49:     let needed = 4 + len;
50:     if cursor + needed > data.len() {
51:         return Err(ArenaError::OutOfSpace);
52:     }
53:     data[cursor..cursor + 4].copy_from_slice(&(len as u32).to_le_bytes());
54:     data[cursor + 4..cursor + needed].copy_from_slice(bytes);
55:     header::set_u32(header, cursor_off, (cursor + needed) as u32);
56:     Ok(cursor as u32)
57: }
58: 
59: /// Allocate a string, returning its arena offset.
60: #[inline]
61: pub(crate) fn alloc_str(
62:     data: &mut [u8],
63:     header: &mut [u8],
64:     s: &str,
65: ) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
66:     alloc(data, header, s.as_bytes())
67: }

69: /// Read the bytes of the entry at `offset` from an arena region.
70: #[inline]

72:     let off = offset as usize;
73:     if off + 4 > data.len() {

75:     }
76:     let len = u32::from_le_bytes(data[off..off + 4].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
77:     if off + 4 + len > data.len() {
78:         return Err(ArenaError::InvalidOffset);
79:     }

14: //! let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
15: //! let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];

38: //! for frame in host.frames() {

79: /// Initialize the linear memory header for a layout. Call once at startup
80: /// before creating a `Guest` or `Host`.
81: pub fn init_memory(mem: &mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) {
82:     header::init(mem, layout);
83: }

85: /// Accessor for a shared-memory ring header, for consumers that read the ring
86: /// in place (zero-copy) without a `Host` handle — e.g. a foreign driver that
87: /// holds a raw pointer to the shared linear memory.
88: ///
89: /// Field offsets match [`memory::OFF_*`] constants and are part of the stable
90: /// wire layout (see `spec/OPCODE.md`).
91: pub struct SharedHeader<'a> {
92:     mem: &'a [u8],
93: }
94: 
95: impl<'a> SharedHeader<'a> {
96:     /// Wrap an immutable view of the shared linear memory.
97:     pub fn new(mem: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
98:         Self { mem }
99:     }
100: 
101:     fn u32(&self, off: usize) -> u32 {
102:         u32::from_le_bytes(self.mem[off..off + 4].try_into().unwrap())
103:     }
104: 
105:     /// `frameCount` — the completed-frame watermark.
106:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
107:         self.u32(memory::OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
108:     }
109: 
110:     /// `readCursor` — the slot the consumer has consumed up to (masked).
111:     pub fn read_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
112:         self.u32(memory::OFF_READ_CURSOR)
113:     }
114: 
115:     /// `writeCursor` — the slot the producer has written up to (masked).
116:     pub fn write_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
117:         self.u32(memory::OFF_WRITE_CURSOR)
118:     }
119: 
120:     /// `slotCount` — number of ring slots (power of two).
121:     pub fn slot_count(&self) -> u32 {
122:         self.u32(memory::OFF_SLOT_COUNT)
123:     }
124: 
125:     /// Byte offset of the ring region within the linear memory.
126:     pub fn ring_offset(&self) -> usize {
127:         self.u32(memory::OFF_RING_OFFSET) as usize
128:     }
129: 
130:     /// Byte length of the ring region.
131:     pub fn ring_bytes(&self) -> usize {
132:         self.u32(memory::OFF_RING_BYTES) as usize
133:     }
134: 
135:     /// Byte offset of the arena region within the linear memory.
136:     pub fn arena_offset(&self) -> usize {
137:         self.u32(memory::OFF_ARENA_OFFSET) as usize
138:     }
139: 
140:     /// Byte offset of the arena cursor.
141:     pub fn arena_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
142:         self.u32(memory::OFF_ARENA_CURSOR)
143:     }
144: }
145: 
146: /// Number of ring slots per the header.
147: fn slot_count(header: &[u8]) -> usize {
148:     header::get_u32(header, OFF_SLOT_COUNT) as usize
149: }
150: 
151: /// Ring mask per the header (slot count is a power of two).
152: fn slot_mask(header: &[u8]) -> usize {
153:     let slots = slot_count(header);
154:     debug_assert!(slots.is_power_of_two());
155:     slots - 1
156: }

159: // Guest (producer)

162: /// Producer side: the guest engine writing opcodes and arena data into shared
163: /// linear memory. Owns the header, ring, and arena regions as disjoint slices.
164: pub struct Guest<'a> {
165:     header: &'a mut [u8],
166:     slots: &'a mut [u8],
167:     /// Host → guest event ring (guest reads raw inputs here).
168:     event_slots: &'a mut [u8],
169:     arena: &'a mut [u8],
170:     /// Host → guest event arena (host-owned bump; the guest resolves `TEXT_CHANGED`
171:     /// text here over the shared ring).
172:     event_arena: &'a mut [u8],
173:     /// Write cursor captured at `begin_frame`.
174:     frame_start: u32,
175: }
176: 
177: impl<'a> Guest<'a> {
178:     /// Create a guest view over the linear memory. `init_memory` MUST have been
179:     /// called on the same memory beforehand.
180:     pub fn new(mem: &'a mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Self {
181:         let (header, rest) = mem.split_at_mut(memory::HEADER_SIZE);
182:         let (slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.ring_bytes());
183:         let (event_slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.event_ring_bytes());
184:         let (arena, event_arena) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.arena_bytes);
185:         let frame_start = header::get_u32(header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
186:         Self {
187:             header,
188:             slots,
189:             event_slots,
190:             arena,
191:             event_arena,
192:             frame_start,
193:         }
194:     }
195: 
196:     fn mask(&self) -> usize {
197:         slot_mask(self.header)
198:     }
199: 
200:     /// Record the start of a new frame.
201:     pub fn begin_frame(&mut self) {
202:         self.frame_start = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
203:     }
204: 
205:     /// Number of opcodes written since the last `begin_frame`.
206:     pub fn pending(&self) -> usize {
207:         let write = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
208:         let mask = self.mask() as u32;
209:         (write.wrapping_sub(self.frame_start) & mask) as usize
210:     }
211: 
212:     /// End the frame: increments `frameCount`.
213:     pub fn end_frame(&mut self) {
214:         let count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
215:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT, count.wrapping_add(1));
216:     }
217: 
218:     /// Total frames produced so far.
219:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
220:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
221:     }

300:     /// Override a design token globally via `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`:

378:     // --- EVENT ingress (host → guest) ---
379: 
380:     /// Drain all pending raw-input events written by the host into the event
381:     /// ring, decoding each 16-byte `EVENT` opcode into a typed [`Event`].
382:     ///
383:     /// The guest (app/engine) polls this to receive renderer-reported inputs.
384:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<Event> {
385:         let mask = self.mask();
386:         let ops = ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask, usize::MAX);
387:         ops.into_iter()
388:             .filter_map(|op| crate::events::decode_event(&op, self.event_arena))
389:             .collect()
390:     }

392:     /// Drain raw `EVENT`-category opcodes from the host → guest event ring as
393:     /// their 16-byte wire form (no decoding). Used by foreign hosts that want
394:     /// the raw bytes.
395:     pub fn drain_event_opcodes(&mut self) -> Vec<Opcode> {
396:         let mask = self.mask();
397:         ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask, usize::MAX)
398:     }
399: 
400:     /// Drain at most `max` raw `EVENT`-category opcodes, leaving the rest
401:     /// pending for a later call (so a caller with a fixed-size buffer never
402:     /// drops events it couldn't copy).
403:     pub fn drain_event_opcodes_max(&mut self, max: usize) -> Vec<Opcode> {
404:         let mask = self.mask();
405:         ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask, max)
406:     }

408:     /// The host → guest event arena bump cursor (diagnostics/tests).
409:     pub fn event_arena_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
410:         header::get_u32(self.header, memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR)
411:     }
412: 
413:     /// Push a raw `EVENT`-category opcode into the host → guest event ring.
414:     ///
415:     /// This is the host-side write (the renderer reporting an input). Exposed
416:     /// here (guest can hold the ring too) so a C-ABI shim can inject raw event
417:     /// opcodes without round-tripping through the typed [`Event`] enum.
418:     pub fn push_event_opcode(&mut self, op: Opcode) -> Result<(), RingError> {
419:         ring_fn::push_event(self.event_slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)
420:     }
421: }

423: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
424: // Host (consumer)
425: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
426: 
427: /// A completed frame produced by the guest: a sequence of opcodes plus arena
428: /// access.
429: ///
430: /// `Frame` is the **transport seam**: both the shared-memory ring (`Host`) and
431: /// network batch decoders produce frame views, so consumers such as
432: /// `RenderTree::apply_frame` work identically regardless of origin.
433: pub struct Frame<'a> {
434:     slots: &'a [u8],
435:     arena: &'a [u8],
436:     start: usize,
437:     end: usize,
438: }
439: 
440: impl<'a> Frame<'a> {
441:     /// Construct a frame view over contiguous 16-byte opcode slots plus an
442:     /// arena region (`start`/`end` are byte offsets into `slots`).
443:     ///
444:     /// Used by transport backends to produce `Frame` views over their own
445:     /// buffers; `Host` builds these internally from the ring.
446:     pub fn from_parts(slots: &'a [u8], arena: &'a [u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> Self {
447:         Self {
448:             slots,
449:             arena,
450:             start,
451:             end,
452:         }
453:     }
454: 
455:     /// Iterate the opcodes in this frame, in order.
456:     pub fn opcodes(&self) -> FrameIter<'a> {
457:         FrameIter {
458:             slots: self.slots,
459:             cursor: self.start,
460:             end: self.end,
461:         }
462:     }
463: 
464:     /// Number of opcodes in the frame.
465:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
466:         (self.end - self.start) / Opcode::SIZE
467:     }
468: 
469:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
470:         self.len() == 0
471:     }
472: 
473:     /// Read an arena entry by offset (see `Guest::alloc` / `Guest::alloc_str`).
474:     pub fn arena_get(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], ArenaError> {
475:         arena_fn::get(self.arena, offset)
476:     }
477: 
478:     /// Read an arena string by offset.
479:     pub fn arena_str(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a str, ArenaError> {
480:         arena_fn::get_str(self.arena, offset)
481:     }
482: 
483:     /// The full arena region (for transport serialization of arena deltas).
484:     pub fn arena(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
485:         self.arena
486:     }
487: }
488: 
489: /// Iterator over the opcodes in a `Frame`.
490: pub struct FrameIter<'a> {
491:     slots: &'a [u8],
492:     cursor: usize,
493:     end: usize,
494: }
495: 
496: impl<'a> Iterator for FrameIter<'a> {
497:     type Item = Opcode;
498: 
499:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Opcode> {
500:         if self.cursor >= self.end {
501:             return None;
502:         }
503:         let bytes: [u8; 16] = self.slots[self.cursor..self.cursor + 16].try_into().unwrap();
504:         self.cursor += 16;
505:         Some(Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes))
506:     }
507: }
508: 
509: /// Consumer side: the host renderer reading completed frames.
510: ///
511: /// SPSC contract: the host never reads past the producer's published
512: /// `writeCursor`, and the producer never overwrites an unconsumed `readCursor`.
513: /// If the host is slow, multiple produced frames are coalesced into one `Frame`
514: /// (opcodes remain in order); the `frameCount` simply signals "new data".
515: pub struct Host<'a> {
516:     header: &'a mut [u8],
517:     slots: &'a [u8],
518:     /// Host → guest event ring (host writes raw inputs here).
519:     event_slots: &'a mut [u8],
520:     arena: &'a [u8],
521:     /// Host → guest event arena (host-owned bump; the host writes event string
522:     /// payloads here, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED` text over the shared ring).
523:     event_arena: &'a mut [u8],
524:     /// Number of frames already consumed by this host view.
525:     consumed: u32,
526: }
527: 
528: impl<'a> Host<'a> {
529:     /// Create a host view over the linear memory.
530:     pub fn new(mem: &'a mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Self {
531:         let (header, rest) = mem.split_at_mut(memory::HEADER_SIZE);
532:         let (slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.ring_bytes());
533:         let (event_slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.event_ring_bytes());
534:         let (arena, event_arena) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.arena_bytes);
535:         let slots: &'a [u8] = slots;
536:         let arena: &'a [u8] = arena;
537:         Self {
538:             header,
539:             slots,
540:             event_slots,
541:             arena,
542:             event_arena,
543:             consumed: 0,
544:         }
545:     }
546: 
547:     /// Total frames produced by the guest (for diagnostics).
548:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
549:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
550:     }
551: 
552:     /// Consume all frames produced since the last call, advancing `readCursor`.
553:     ///
554:     /// Returns at most one `Frame` (all new opcodes since the last drain). If
555:     /// the producer produced multiple frames before this call they coalesce.
556:     pub fn frames(&mut self) -> Vec<Frame<'a>> {
557:         let frame_count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
558:         if self.consumed >= frame_count {
559:             return Vec::new();
560:         }
561:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
562:         let start = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, mask);
563:         let end = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
564: 
565:         // The masked write cursor can wrap past the read cursor (the producer
566:         // laps the reader numerically). The pending run is counted modulo the
567:         // ring size; a plain `end < start` guard would permanently deadlock the
568:         // ring at the wrap boundary (the reader never advances again). A
569:         // wrapped run is drained in two calls — first the [start..slots) head,
570:         // then the [0..end) tail — advancing `readCursor` between them, so the
571:         // opcodes still reach the consumer in ring order.
572:         let count = end.wrapping_sub(start) & mask;
573:         if count == 0 {
574:             return Vec::new();
575:         }
576:         let run_end = (start + count) & mask; // exclusive slot index of the full run
577:         let (drain_to_slot, frame_byte_end) = if run_end > start {
578:             (run_end, run_end * Opcode::SIZE)
579:         } else {
580:             (0, self.slots.len()) // wrapped: drain the head now, the tail next call
581:         };
582: 
583:         let frames = vec![Frame {
584:             slots: self.slots,
585:             arena: self.arena,
586:             start: start * Opcode::SIZE,
587:             end: frame_byte_end,
588:         }];
589: 
590:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, drain_to_slot as u32);
591:         self.consumed = frame_count;
592: 
593:         // A `META::RESET` invalidates prior state: reset the host → guest event
594:         // arena cursor so the host starts bump-allocating fresh (matching the
595:         // guest arena's reset-on-RESET semantics).
596:         let drained_end_byte = if drain_to_slot > start {
597:             drain_to_slot * Opcode::SIZE
598:         } else {
599:             self.slots.len() // wrapped head: drained [start .. ring end)
600:         };
601:         let reset_seen = self.slots[start * Opcode::SIZE..drained_end_byte]
602:             .chunks_exact(Opcode::SIZE)
603:             .any(|slot| {
604:                 let bytes: [u8; 16] = slot.try_into().unwrap();
605:                 let op = Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes);
606:                 op.category() == category::META && op.command() == crate::meta::RESET
607:             });
608:         if reset_seen {
609:             memory::header::set_u32(self.header, memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR, 0);
610:         }
611: 
612:         frames
613:     }
614: 
615:     /// Write a raw-input event (host → guest) into the event ring, encoded as a
616:     /// 16-byte `EVENT` opcode. The renderer reports inputs here; the guest
617:     /// drains them via [`Guest::drain_events`].
618:     ///
619:     /// `TextChanged` text and `Navigate` URLs are bump-allocated into the
620:     /// host → guest **event arena** and referenced by their absolute offset in
621:     /// `B` (the `SET_TEXT` shared-memory convention); the guest resolves them
622:     /// from the same region. If the event arena is full the event is rejected
623:     /// with [`RingError::Full`] (backpressure).
624:     pub fn send_event(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), RingError> {
625:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
626:         let op = match event {
627:             Event::TextChanged { target, value } => {
628:                 let offset = crate::arena::alloc_event(&mut self.event_arena, self.header, value.as_bytes())
629:                     .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
630:                 Opcode::new(category::EVENT, crate::event::TEXT_CHANGED, 0, *target, offset, 0)
631:             }
632:             Event::Navigate { url: Some(url) } => {
633:                 let offset = crate::arena::alloc_event(&mut self.event_arena, self.header, url.as_bytes())
634:                     .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
635:                 Opcode::new(
636:                     category::EVENT,
637:                     crate::event::NAVIGATE,
638:                     crate::flag::NAVIGATE_URL,
639:                     0,
640:                     offset,
641:                     0,
642:                 )
643:             }
644:             _ => event.encode(),
645:         };
646:         ring_fn::push_event(self.event_slots, self.header, mask, &op)
647:     }
648: }

838:             slot_count: 4,
839:             arena_bytes: MemoryLayout::default().arena_bytes,
840:             event_arena_bytes: MemoryLayout::default().event_arena_bytes,
841:         };
842:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
843:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
844: 
845:         // Guest writes three opcodes (slots 0,1,2; capacity is slot_count-1).
846:         {
847:             let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
848:             guest.begin_frame();
849:             guest.create_node(1, component_type::VSTACK).unwrap();
850:             guest.create_node(2, component_type::HSTACK).unwrap();
851:             guest.create_node(3, component_type::TEXT).unwrap();
852:             guest.end_frame();
853:         }
854:         // Host drains everything -> readCursor = 3.
855:         {
856:             let mut host = Host::new(&mut mem, &layout);
857:             assert_eq!(host.frames().len(), 1);
858:         }
859:         // Guest writes one more opcode -> slot 3, writeCursor wraps 3 -> 0.
860:         // Now masked write(0) < masked read(3) — the wrap that used to
861:         // permanently deadlock the frame ring.
862:         {
863:             let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
864:             guest.begin_frame();
865:             guest.create_node(4, component_type::TEXT).unwrap();
866:             guest.end_frame();

868: 
869:         // The wrapped run is the head [3..4) + a (here empty) tail [0..0): the
870:         // first read drains the head in ring order...
871:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut mem, &layout);
872:         let frames = host.frames();
873:         assert_eq!(frames.len(), 1);
874:         assert_eq!(frames[0].opcodes().count(), 1);
875:         assert_eq!(frames[0].opcodes().next().unwrap().a(), 4);
876:         // ...and readCursor advanced to 0, so nothing is left pending.
877:         assert!(host.frames().is_empty());
878:         // And the producer can wrap again without ever deadlocking.
879:         {
880:             let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
881:             guest.begin_frame();
882:             guest.create_node(5, component_type::TEXT).unwrap();
883:             guest.end_frame();
884:         }
885:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut mem, &layout);
886:         assert_eq!(host.frames()[0].opcodes().next().unwrap().a(), 5);

3: //! These constants are part of the wire protocol (see `spec/OPCODE.md`) and MUST

7: /// Opcode categories (`Category` field, u8).
8: pub mod category {
9:     /// Tree mutations (guest → host): node create/delete/insert/remove/move.
10:     pub const TREE: u8 = 0x01;

12:     /// (spacing, padding, alignment, …) and content that native renderers use
13:     /// to lay out and style native elements. The engine does NOT emit rects.
14:     pub const PARAMETER: u8 = 0x02;
15:     /// Raw input events (host → guest): pointer down/move/up, key down/up.
16:     pub const EVENT: u8 = 0x03;
17:     /// Control (both directions): reset, environment, custom data.
18:     pub const META: u8 = 0x04;
19: }

113: pub mod meta {
114:     /// Host must clear all rendered output.
115:     pub const RESET: u8 = 0x01;

119:     pub const ENVIRONMENT: u8 = 0x02;

125:     /// heartbeat): the shared-memory ring MUST NOT emit, expect, or relay it.
126:     pub const PING: u8 = 0x04;

1: //! Producer-side ring helpers operating on the ring region and header cursors.
2: //!
3: //! The ring is a power-of-two slot array. The guest writes at `writeCursor` and
4: //! the host reads from `readCursor`. Both cursors live in the header block.

11: /// Errors produced by the ring producer.
12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
13: pub enum RingError {
14:     /// The ring is full (consumer has not caught up). The producer SHOULD
15:     /// publish a frame before emitting further opcodes.
16:     Full,
17: }

19: /// Append `op` to the ring at `writeCursor` and advance the cursor.
20: ///
21: /// `slots` is the full ring region; `mask` wraps the cursor. Fails with
22: /// `RingError::Full` when the next slot equals `readCursor`.
23: #[inline]
24: pub(crate) fn push(slots: &mut [u8], header: &mut [u8], mask: usize, op: &Opcode) -> Result<(), RingError> {
25:     let write = cursor(header, memory::OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
26:     let next = (write + 1) & mask;
27:     if next == cursor(header, memory::OFF_READ_CURSOR, mask) {
28:         return Err(RingError::Full);
29:     }
30:     let bytes = op.to_bytes();
31:     let off = write * Opcode::SIZE;
32:     slots[off..off + Opcode::SIZE].copy_from_slice(&bytes);
33:     header::set_u32(header, memory::OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, next as u32);
34:     Ok(())
35: }

228:     let off = write * Opcode::SIZE;
229:     event_slots[off..off + Opcode::SIZE].copy_from_slice(&bytes);
230:     header::set_u32(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_WRITE_CURSOR, next as u32);
231:     Ok(())
232: }

234: /// Drain pending `EVENT`-category opcodes from the host → guest event ring,
235: /// advancing `eventReadCursor`. The guest (app/engine) reads raw inputs here.
236: ///
237: /// The masked cursors wrap independently — the writer can lap the reader
238: /// numerically — so the pending count is computed modulo the ring size. A
239: /// plain `write < read` guard would permanently deadlock the ring the moment
240: /// the writer wraps past the reader (the reader never advances, the writer is
241: /// stuck "full", and every drain returns empty). `max` bounds how many opcodes
242: /// are drained (the rest stay pending for the next call).
243: #[inline]
244: pub(crate) fn read_events(
245:     event_slots: &[u8],
246:     header: &mut [u8],
247:     mask: usize,
248:     max: usize,
249: ) -> Vec<Opcode> {
250:     let read = cursor(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_READ_CURSOR, mask);
251:     let write = cursor(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
252:     let count = write.wrapping_sub(read) & mask;
253:     let n = count.min(max);
254:     if n == 0 {
255:         return Vec::new();
256:     }
257:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n);
258:     for i in 0..n {
259:         let slot = (read + i) & mask;
260:         let off = slot * Opcode::SIZE;
261:         let bytes: [u8; Opcode::SIZE] =
262:             event_slots[off..off + Opcode::SIZE].try_into().unwrap();
263:         out.push(Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes));
264:     }
265:     header::set_u32(header, memory::OFF_EVENT_READ_CURSOR, ((read + n) & mask) as u32);
266:     out
267: }
